title: Auto-shim and compatibility scanner for canary tool-calls
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a compatibility scanner and temporary adapter/shim generator that runs during canary and shadow rollouts to detect and mitigate breaking structured-output and function-call interface changes. The scanner will compute fine-grained diffs of call signatures and payload shapes, estimate impact, and optionally generate a zero-touch shim to translate new outputs back to the prev-compatible shape until a rollout is validated or automatically rolled back.
background: We frequently onboard newer model versions that change function-call shapes (parameter renames, optional->required, nested schema changes) which cause downstream runtime errors and customer-visible regressions during rollouts. Existing probes detect shape diffs but require manual mitigation. This ticket aims to automate detection, produce human-readable diffs, and in low-risk cases create temporary shims that preserve backward compatibility during the canary window. If regressions exceed thresholds, the system should trigger auto rollback per the rollout policy.
proposed_solution: 1) Compatibility scanner that runs against traffic samples during shadow and canary phases. It will compare actual model outputs to the currently pinned contract using a deterministic signature/shape comparison and semantic checks (required field addition, type changes, enum deltas). 2) Shim generator that synthesizes translation rules (rename, default inject, type coerce, optional unwrap) and emits a self-contained adapter deployed alongside the new model variant. 3) Risk scorer that maps diffs to a severity score and triggers auto-revert if severity > threshold or if downstream integration tests fail. 4) Integrate results into the Console: per-rollout diff UI, suggested shim code, and one-click apply/revert actions.
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Auto-shims can mask incompatible behavior and delay necessary model fixes; limit to low-risk transformations (renames, defaults, safe coercions).
- Synthesized coercions must be auditable and time-limited; annotate each shim with TTL and origin.
- Performance: runtime adapter adds small latency; prefer applying shim in the routing layer for canary slices only.
- Security: shims must not create privilege escalation or leak data; require security review and signed artifacts for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility scanner runs as part of shadow and canary workflows and produces structured diffs for 100% of sampled invocations.
Shim generator can produce a runnable adapter (Node/Python) for the top 3 low-risk diff patterns automatically.
Console shows a per-rollout diff panel with severity scores and a button to apply or revoke the shim.
Auto-rollback triggers when severity score or downstream integration failure rate exceeds configured thresholds and completes within rollout timeout.
Generated shims include TTL metadata and an audit entry in the rollout trace log.
technical_notes: Compatibility fingerprinting: use ordered canonicalization of JSON schema + function signature hashes to create compact fingerprints for quick equality checks.
Diff taxonomy: addition_optional, addition_required, removal, type_change, enum_delta, nested_shape_change. Each mapped to a severity weight.
Shim DSL: small rule language that supports field_rename, default_inject, type_coerce, enum_map, and path_mapping. DSL compiled to Node/Python wrappers for runtime use.
Placement: router-side adapter preferred for minimal model runtime changes. For Dedicated/Private, support deploying shim as a sidecar in customer runtime with signed bundle.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary infra): implement scanner that runs offline on recorded canary_samples and posts diffs to rollout API (2 sprints).
Phase 2 (shim MVP): implement DSL and generator for 3 basic patterns and add apply/revoke flow in Console (2 sprints).
Phase 3 (policy+auto-rollback): implement severity scoring and integrate with rollout orchestration for auto-revert, metrics and incident playbook (1 sprint).
Phase 4 (hardening): expand pattern coverage, security review, and private deployment signing (1 sprint).
test_plan: Unit tests for diff engine covering >80 patterns and edge cases (nulls, arrays, nested maps).
E2E test: synthetic models that emit controlled schema deltas; verify scanner, shim, and rollback behavior on canary pipeline.
Load test: measure added latency for router-side shim under 99th percentile load; target <3ms additional p50 and <15ms p99.
Compatibility matrix tests for node/python shim artifacts on Dedicated and Private deployment images.
monitoring_and_alerts: New rollout telemetry: diff_count, severity_histogram, shim_applied_count, shim_ttl_expirations, auto_revert_count.
Alert: severity_score > 70 for any canary slice for >5min -> Pager on-call infra.
Dashboard: per-model and per-route compatibility heatmap and recent rollback timeline.
Audit logs: each generated shim and apply/revert action stored with user/actor, timestamp, and link to PR or symlink.
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with PM and Design. Agreed to limit auto-shim to safe transformations and surface all shims in Console.
2026-02-25: Prototype diff engine ready; initial taxonomy validated against 30 recent rollouts. Found common pattern: field rename + optional wrap.
2026-03-03: Implemented DSL prototype and generator for field_rename and default_inject. Generated shim applied in local router test harness.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed shim DSL; flagged requirement for signed shim bundles for Private deployments. Added to Phase 4.
2026-03-12: Added severity scoring draft and integrated with canary abort API; E2E tests planned for next week.
open_questions: What transformations should be considered 'low-risk' by default and which require explicit human approval?
Do we store generated shim bundles indefinitely or auto-expire them after TTL? Default TTL proposed: 72 hours.
What's the UX for showing suggested shim diffs to an on-call engineer vs auto-applying? Should auto-apply be opt-in per org?
